chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The inheritance of the child of mulāʿanah belongs to his mother. If his mother is not alive, then it goes to the closest people from his mother’s side, his maternal uncles.

key_terms.أَقْرَبِ النَّاسِ: the nearest relatives in line of kinship
key_terms.مِيرَاثَ: inheritance; the estate to be distributed
key_terms.وَلَدِ الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: the child of mulāʿanah, i.e. a child legally affected by mutual imprecation/liʿān

ai.seo_question: Who inherits from the child of mulāʿanah according to Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the inheritance of a child connected to liʿān/mulāʿanah. It states that his estate goes to his mother, and if she has died, then it passes to the nearest of her relatives, specifically the maternal uncles.
